title: A node can be placed at a point along another node's side
body:
Today `at NAME DX DY` starts from the named thing's top-left corner, and a connector's end can be the middle of a side or a corner. Nothing names a point a fraction of the way along a side, and nothing puts a node's centre at a point. The sufr pipeline figure in `sufr-figures` centres a strip under each quarter of a text bar, which takes arithmetic on the bar's left edge and width in every `at`.

## Proposal

- `at`, `from` and `to` take `NAME SIDE F`, the point F of the way along that side, left to right or top to bottom. `bar bottom 0.375` is the middle of the bar's second quarter, on its bottom edge.
- A node takes `place CORNER | SIDE | center`, the point of its own box that `at` puts down. The default is `top-left`, as today.

```text
row strip2 { at bar bottom 0.375 0 30; place top; unit 24 24; chars "%ACGNT"; }
```

## Open

- `anchor` already names the point of a node that stays put when a timeline scales it. `place` would be a second property of the same shape, and one property might do both.
close_reason: Landed in ace7ffe on dev: `at NAME SIDE F` and `SIDE F` in `from`/`to` through `along_side` and `at_named` in `scene/build.rs`, and `place` on box, ellipse, row, matrix, code, text and math through `placed`. The syntax is logged on acre-4518a5.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/0c799e42
notes.text: Jack accepted on 2026-11-23, provisionally: `place` is a property of its own, apart from `anchor`. Merging them would change the default of `anchor` and move existing figures.
